title: Strict monotonicity of the biased minus probability
statement: Let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be monotone and nonconstant. For $p,q\in[0,1]$ with $p<q$, choose each coordinate independently to equal $-1$ with probability $p$ or $q$, respectively. Then the probability that $f$ equals $-1$ under parameter $p$ is strictly less than under parameter $q$.
